title: Canvas
summary: A pan and zoom ground for design tools: the slotted content (a page, a drawing, a diagram) sits in a world that you drag, scroll or pinch around and zoom with Ctrl and the wheel, the plus and minus buttons or the keyboard, over an optional grid. A coordinate API (pointToWorld, worldToPoint) converts between screen and world units and snaps to the grid, and nodes the page flags with data-surface-selected get a selection frame that follows the view. The surface reports what happened (pk-view-change, pk-canvas-pick, pk-canvas-key) and never changes your content: the page owns the selection.

props.name: zoom
props.description: The scale of the world: 1 is actual size. Clamped between minZoom and maxZoom by the user's gestures; setting it from the page is taken as is.

props.name: panX
props.description: Where the world origin sits horizontally, in pixels from the left edge of the surface.

props.name: panY
props.description: Where the world origin sits vertically, in pixels from the top edge of the surface.

props.name: grid
props.description: The grid spacing in world units, drawn behind the content and scaled with the zoom; 0 draws none. pointToWorld snaps to it.

props.name: minZoom
props.description: The smallest scale a gesture or button can reach.

props.name: maxZoom
props.description: The largest scale a gesture or button can reach.

props.name: label
props.description: The surface's accessible name (it is a focusable group). Required.

slots.description: The content being edited. It is placed at the world origin and takes the world's pan and zoom. Add data-surface-selected to a descendant to frame it as selected.

events.name: pk-view-change
events.description: The user panned or zoomed (drag, wheel, pinch, keys, buttons).

events.name: pk-canvas-pick
events.description: A press without movement: target is the deepest content node under it, or null on the bare ground; additive when Shift, Ctrl or Cmd was held. The page decides what to select.

events.name: pk-canvas-key
events.description: Delete, Escape or Shift with an arrow on the focused surface, for the page to act on (plain arrows pan, + and - zoom, 0 resets).

parts.name: frame
parts.description: The focusable ground that clips, pans and draws the grid

parts.name: world
parts.description: The layer that carries the slotted content under the pan and zoom transform

parts.name: overlay
parts.description: The marks layer (pointer-events none): one frame per node flagged data-surface-selected

parts.name: mark
parts.description: The hidden template of the frame drawn around a flagged node; the surface clones it into the overlay

parts.name: toolbar
parts.description: The zoom out, zoom in and reset buttons

cssProperties.name: --pk-canvas-bg
cssProperties.default: a mix of the page background and text

cssProperties.name: --pk-canvas-grid
cssProperties.default: a faint mix of the text colour

cssProperties.name: --pk-canvas-width
cssProperties.description: The width of the world the content is laid out in, at zoom 1

methods.name: pointToWorld(clientX, clientY)
methods.description: Returns { x, y } in world units for a point on the screen, snapped to the grid when there is one

methods.name: worldToPoint(x, y)
methods.description: Returns { x, y } in client pixels for a world point

methods.name: reset()
methods.description: Back to zoom 1 at the origin (announces pk-view-change)

a11y: The surface is a labelled group and a single tab stop. With focus on it the arrow keys pan, + and - zoom, 0 resets the view, and Delete, Escape and Shift with an arrow are reported as pk-canvas-key so the page can offer an accessible way to select and edit. The toolbar buttons keep their names when they fold to icons. The selection frames are decoration (aria-hidden): the page announces the selection itself. The slotted content stays in the reading order and remains focusable.
mobile: Touch: one finger drags the ground to pan, two fingers pinch to zoom around their midpoint, a tap picks. The page does not scroll under the gesture (touch-action none), and the toolbar buttons fold to icons at phone width with a 44px target.
